title: Value-Added Services Clause — Alternative Rides after a Late Value-Added Leg on RideLink
content:
An alternative ride after a late pickup under Non-Emergency Medical Transportation is paid in full for a medical leg, and at a share of the fare for a value-added leg.

**Rule.** The share of the fare paid follows the kind of leg: a value-added leg of a benefit year whose allotment load entries carried more trips than its debit entries used is paid the covered value-added share of 0.9 of the fare; any other value-added leg is paid the uncovered value-added share of 0.5; a medical leg is paid in full. The fare is multiplied by the leg's share before it is compared with the claim's cap.

A value-added leg is one whose registered trip purpose is pharmacy, WIC, food bank or community health class; every other purpose makes a medical leg. The benefit year is the calendar year of the late leg's trip date, and the loaded and used trips are read from that year's allotment load entries and debit entries on the value-added trip ledger.

## Decision table

| Late leg | That year's loaded trips compared with its used trips | Share of the fare |
|---|---|---|
| Value-added | Loaded more than used | 0.9 |
| Value-added | Loaded equal to or fewer than used, or no load entry | 0.5 |
| Medical | Any | Full |

## Cases

*Hypothetical late legs:*

- A pharmacy leg in a year with 24 trips loaded and 10 used: 0.9 of the fare.
- A food-bank leg in a year with 12 trips loaded and 12 used: 0.5 of the fare.
- A WIC leg in a year with no allotment load entry and no trips used: loaded does not exceed used, so 0.5.
- A dialysis leg: paid in full.

*Worked figure, hypothetical:* a fare of 40.00 USD on a covered value-added leg becomes 36.00 USD before any cap.
